name: Signed/Unsigned Conversion Poisons a Shared Aggregate
essence: A negative refund cast to unsigned is added, under a lock, to the shared balance.

examples.summary: A refund of -1 becomes 4294967295 and is added to the locked balance.
examples.mechanism: as u32 reinterprets the i32 bit pattern. The Mutex makes the addition race-free and does not recover the sign (CWE-195, CWE-682). The ledger is u64 so the poisoned add does not wrap.

ingredients.suggests: The negative refund is cast to an unsigned credit before addition.
Every ledger update must acquire the single shared ledger Mutex.

examples.summary: A refund becomes a huge credit while competing callers share a single posting slot.
examples.mechanism: The >>> 0 escape hatch converts -1 to 4294967295; concurrent posting attempts contend for one slot, and the accepted posting adds that unsigned value to the shared balance.
examples.expected_behavior: The accepted refund leaves balance 99; excess work is queued or reported busy.

ingredients.suggests: The negative refund is converted to an unsigned 32-bit credit.
Two refund calls contend for one shared posting slot held across an await.
evidence: if (inFlight > POSTING_CAPACITY) throw new Error("ledger busy");
